articleText:
[Hacker News — afr.com]
Maani Truu Education correspondent Updated Sep 23, 2026 – 1.14pm , first published at 12.00pm An Australian tutoring company has told parents to invest in Gemini or ChatGPT rather than pay overpriced human tutors to give their children an academic edge, as students increasingly turn to artificial intelligence for exam preparation and immediate study feedback.

Dymocks Tutoring and Talent 100, which has five centres across Sydney, will close at the end of the week after telling customers that technology has rendered its service obsolete.

reactions: [Hacker News] disagree- i used it for the last few years of coursework preparing for exams. If you give it context (i'm studying for an exam, do not give hints unless asked, your objective is to help my understanding) it is incredibly helpful. This isn't advice, it's a company going out of business.
[Hacker News] As a teacher, this is obvious. But when you ask a student 'do you want to learn?' they don't actually understand the question.
[Hacker News] A calculator, Youtube and iPad tried to replace teachers. They all failed but this time it's different.

[Hacker News] I'm all for saving money where you can, but these models really aren't great for learning because they love giving you answers and it's so easy to get an answer, but the process to get to the answer is how you actually learn. Unless you put guardrails in place to actually learn, I don't think this advice is good.

items.title: Tutoring company tells parents to save their money and 'use AI instead'
Australian school tutoring company shuts down, tells parents to save their money and ‘use AI instead’
